SPORTS · NDTV Sports · editor 6/10 · 1 min read fact-checked

India Secures 12th Gold at Asian Games 2026; Medal Tally Reaches 70

India's medal tally at the Asian Games 2026 reached 70 on Day 13, including 12 gold, 24 silver, and 35 bronze medals, placing the nation sixth in the standings. Boxer Lovlina Borgohain secured the 12th gold, defeating China's Bao Ziyi 5-0 in the women's 75kg final, becoming only the second Indian woman after MC Mary Kom to achieve an Asian Games boxing gold. Earlier, the Indian women's recurve archery team, comprising Ankita Bhakat, Kirti, and Kumkum Mohod, clinched its maiden Asian Games gold by beating South Korea.

Wrestler Sujeet advanced to the men's 65kg final after defeating Japan's Kotaro Kiyooka and is set to compete for gold against Abdulmazhid Kudiev of Tajikistan at 2:46 p.m. IST. In other medal events, the recurve mixed team, featuring Dhiraj Bommadevara and Kumkum Mohod, earned a silver medal after losing to China. Additionally, Nethra Kumanan secured a bronze medal in the women's dinghy sailing event.

Dipanshi (50kg wrestling) will contend for a bronze medal via repechage at 3:58 p.m. IST against Kazakhstan's Zeinep Bayanova, having defeated Cambodia's Samnang Dit. India's women's hockey team will also play China for a gold medal. Parveen and Ankush are scheduled for their respective boxing gold medal bouts. In rugby sevens, India defeated Malaysia 26-5 in the women's Pool E match, moving into the 5th-8th classification round.

What to watch: India's final medal count and position as the Games conclude.

ENTERTAINMENT · Bollywood Hungama · editor 9/10 · 1 min read fact-checked

Drishyam The Conclusion Sparks Pre-Release Midnight Shows, High Ticket Pricing

Drishyam The Conclusion, the third installment of the franchise, is set for a historic opening today, October 2. The Ajay Devgn-led thriller is experiencing tremendous demand, prompting exhibitors to schedule post-midnight and early morning shows even before its release day.

Unlike Drishyam 2 in November 2022, where such shows were often added later on opening day, exhibitors have acted proactively this time. Several Mumbai cinemas, including PVR Lower Parel, Cinepolis Seawoods, and Metro Inox, have opened bookings for post-midnight shows as early as October 1. Maxus Bhayander has gone further, scheduling shows practically round the clock at 12:35 am, 1:05 am, 2:05 am, 3:05 am, 4:05 am, and 5:05 am. This trend is also evident in Pune, with venues like Inox Megaplex Wakad, and in Ahmedabad at locations such as Connplex Prahladnagar.

The unprecedented demand has also led to high ticket pricing. Exhibition sources indicate that theatres have been asked to price tickets for Drishyam The Conclusion on par with major releases like Spider-Man: Brand New Day and Dhurandhar The Revenge. The film was cleared by the CBFC without any cuts and is 8 minutes longer than Drishyam 2.

What to watch: The film's opening box office performance.

SCIENCE BRIEF · BBC Science · editor 6/10 · 1 min read fact-checked

UK Farmers Criticize Sustainable Farming Initiative Funding Scramble

Farmers are expressing frustration after a £253m government funding window for the Sustainable Farming Initiative closed in less than six hours. Norfolk farmer Lex Brun reported missing out on a £100,000 grant, forcing him to reconsider environmental projects in favor of commercial crops due to rising costs.

Farming Minister Stephen Morgan acknowledged the disappointment and promised to learn from the application process, while the Country Land and Business Association warned of reduced environmental engagement. As the government considers future support, politicians and agricultural groups are calling for continued investment to ensure long-term confidence in green land management schemes.

Election Commission Orders Targeted Voter Roll Verification

The Election Commission has directed Booth Level Officers in 20 states and Union Territories to compare pre- and post-SIR electoral rolls to identify missing voters. BLOs must conduct house-to-house visits to verify the status of these individuals and assist eligible citizens in filing Form 6 for re-enrolment.

The month-long exercise requires BLOs to share booth-wise lists of missing electors with political party representatives to facilitate transparency. This directive, part of a broader drive to enroll first-time and left-out voters, aims to rectify discrepancies identified after the Special Intensive Revision process.

Trump Threatens Retaliation if Iran Linked to Flight Attack

President Donald Trump warned that Iran will be hit "very hard" if investigators confirm Tehran's involvement in a FlyDubai copilot's attempt to crash an Israel-bound jet. The copilot reportedly stabbed the captain, causing the plane to plummet before passengers intervened and forced a landing in Saudi Arabia.

While Trump stated the U.S. is currently investigating potential ties between the attacker and Iran, diplomatic efforts to end the seven-month war remain stalled. Meanwhile, the U.S. military has deployed approximately 9,000 troops and three aircraft carriers to the West Asia region amid heightened tensions.

NATIONAL BRIEF · The Hindu · editor 9/10 · 1 min read fact-checked

ECI Orders BLOs to Re-enroll Eligible Voters Omitted from Lists

The Election Commission of India (ECI) has directed Booth Level Officers (BLOs) to compare pre-Special Intensive Revision (SIR) voter lists with current records to identify eligible electors who were inadvertently left out. BLOs must conduct house-to-house visits to verify status and facilitate re-enrollment through Form 6.

Officials are instructed to cover at least 20-25 electors weekly, aiming to complete the process within one month. The initiative includes organizing booth-level camps and special outreach for marginalized groups, including those in labor colonies and night shelters, to ensure all eligible citizens are correctly registered.

Source: The Hindu · permalink · more national

Delhi Police Restrict Protests Against CEC Gyanesh Kumar

Authorities have heightened security and suspended internet services around Delhi’s Jantar Mantar following a denied protest permit against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Police barricaded the site and detained Aam Aadmi Party leader Saurabh Bharadwaj as crowds gathered on Gandhi Jayanti.

Delhi Traffic Police issued an advisory warning of diversions near Connaught Place and Parliament Street, urging commuters to avoid the area. Concurrently, Citizens for Justice and Peace founder Abhijeet Dipke faces similar restrictions for a planned demonstration at Mumbai’s Shivaji Park, as activists continue to demand the CEC’s resignation.
